chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
We mentioned the plucking from the moustache, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a good display, and it is from the Sunnah'.

key_terms.نُشْرَةٌ: A good display / beauty / enhancement of appearance

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on plucking the moustache according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies that the moustache should be 'nushrah' (lightly trimmed or plucked) rather than completely removed, distinguishing it from the fuller beard which is to be kept. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining a distinct masculine appearance in accordance with the Sunnah, contrasting with the practice of some other schools that may advocate for complete removal. The term 'Sunnah' here indicates a recommended act (mustahabb) that carries spiritual and social significance in Islamic grooming etiquette.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘We mentioned the plucking from the moustache, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a good display, and it is from the Sunnah’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Once we mentioned trimming the mustache before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a charm and trimming it is of Sunnah.”’
